scope: Historical audit of the original candidates in runs 29-58, as accepted by the user. REGENERATE and MISSING decisions do not review replacement images or pending pilots.
method: All five reviews/images-*.jpg contact sheets inspected with view_image; originals 35, 37, 42, 54 and 55 additionally inspected at full image resolution. Prior PASS files were not treated as engagement evidence.
criteria: Ages 4+ starting school: engaging recognizable subjects, bold flat colors and reasonably large paintable regions.
Target roughly six to ten genuinely distinct colors in meaningful areas, with repeated interesting number regions.
Do not inflate palette with white background, black ink, tiny highlights or similar shades.
Preserve user-approved toucan 35 as the benchmark; cow 37 also explicitly approved by the user.
Generated number placement was not inspected.

decisions.subject: Puppy
decisions.reason: Tan dominates; turquoise accessory adds little variety.
decisions.suggestion: Add a striped bandana, multicolored ball and contrasting patches with large enclosed regions.

decisions.subject: Penguin
decisions.reason: Orange and pale blue provide little color activity.
decisions.suggestion: Add a broad striped scarf, colorful hat and simple fish.

decisions.subject: Kangaroo
decisions.reason: Almost entirely orange/tan; joey repeats the same palette.
decisions.suggestion: Add a colorful pouch decoration, scarf and a few large flowers.

decisions.subject: Snail
decisions.reason: Only three meaningful colors; spiral does not create enough enclosed regions.
decisions.suggestion: Use a segmented rainbow shell and large leaf/flower shapes.

decisions.subject: Butterfly
decisions.reason: Good symmetry and repeated regions, but only four colors.
decisions.suggestion: Preserve silhouette; add large mirrored wing patches using six to eight colors.

decisions.subject: Octopus
decisions.reason: Essentially one purple region.
decisions.suggestion: Add broad contrasting arm sections, large spots and simple colorful underwater objects.

decisions.subject: Toucan
observations: User-approved engagement benchmark: the oversized two-tone beak and yellow face provide strong focal color, supported by substantial green leaves, blue feet and a brown branch.
Three separate leaves and two feet repeat color choices across recognizable regions; the broad body and beak remain accessible for ages 4+.
KEEP is based on composition and meaningful paintable variety, not an inflated count of background white, black ink, highlights or neighboring orange shades.

decisions.subject: Sheep
decisions.reason: Cream wool, peach face and brown legs offer very little activity.
decisions.suggestion: Add a broad patterned blanket, colorful flowers and distinct large wool sections.

decisions.subject: Cow
observations: Explicitly user-approved keeper: substantial pink muzzle and inner ears, teal collar and yellow bell add meaningful color to the cream and brown animal.
Repeated body patches, paired inner ears and four hooves provide separate regions for repeated number/color matching.
Palette breadth is borderline, but recognizable anatomy, large patches and substantial accessory colors make the activity engaging without relying on bell shading or tiny facial details.

decisions.subject: Hedgehog
decisions.reason: Mostly two animal colors plus red apple; green leaf is minor.
decisions.suggestion: Add large contrasting spine sections and a few colorful garden objects.

decisions.subject: Seal
decisions.reason: Huge gray body; three ball colors carry nearly all the interest.
decisions.suggestion: Add a broad striped scarf and additional large ball panels or simple beach props.

decisions.subject: Camel
decisions.reason: Yellow body and turquoise blanket dominate.
decisions.suggestion: Give the blanket large multicolored panels and add a contrasting halter and simple desert plants.

decisions.subject: Rocket
decisions.reason: Repeated fins help, but palette and body subdivision remain limited.
decisions.suggestion: Add blue body panels, a purple window surround and distinct broad flame sections.

decisions.subject: Hot-air balloon
observations: Five broad orange, yellow, green, blue and purple balloon panels plus a substantial brown basket provide six meaningful color families.
Large enclosed panels are highly accessible for ages 4+; basket and its rims repeat brown across separate regions.
Accepted as an easier entry with fewer repeated regions than the strongest keepers; background and thin suspension ropes do not inflate the palette.

decisions.subject: Train
observations: Red cab and chassis, blue boiler, yellow chimney and front, contrasting orange and green wheels, gray wheel/rail and a lighter blue window distribute color across recognizable components.
Repeated red body sections, yellow fittings and distinct wheels support number/color matching in reasonably large regions.
Engagement comes from substantial machine components rather than black outlines, tiny hubs or white background; the subject remains immediately recognizable.

decisions.subject: Aeroplane
decisions.reason: Yellow dominates; neighboring blues do not supply enough variety.
decisions.suggestion: Add contrasting wing panels, tail stripes and large colored propeller blades.

decisions.subject: Excavator
decisions.reason: Mostly yellow, blue and dark gray; tracks introduce fiddly detail.
decisions.suggestion: Simplify tracks and add large contrasting machine panels and colorful construction objects.

decisions.subject: Camping tent
decisions.reason: Four main colors, with most area in one coral triangle.
decisions.suggestion: Add broad tent panels, a contrasting groundsheet and a simple colorful lantern.

decisions.subject: Beach bucket
decisions.reason: Mostly blue, red and yellow; sand contributes little contrast.
decisions.suggestion: Add large bucket decorations and substantial contrasting shells or beach toys.

decisions.subject: Cupcake
decisions.reason: Pink frosting and turquoise wrapper dominate; cherry stem cannot count as meaningful green.
decisions.suggestion: Use alternating wrapper panels and several large frosting decorations.

decisions.subject: Ice cream
decisions.reason: Four large regions with almost no repeated matching.
decisions.suggestion: Add broad sauce sections, chunky enclosed cone panels and a colorful wafer.

decisions.subject: Teapot
decisions.reason: Three meaningful colors despite multiple parts.
decisions.suggestion: Repeat large contrasting motifs across pot and cup; introduce a distinct saucer and lid sections.

decisions.subject: Watering can
decisions.reason: Three main colors; flower repeats yellow throughout.
decisions.suggestion: Use contrasting large petals, center and can panels, plus a simple potted plant.

decisions.subject: Rain boots
decisions.reason: Yellow boots and coral umbrella dominate; only four meaningful colors.
decisions.suggestion: Add repeated broad boot patches and alternating umbrella panels.

decisions.subject: Present
decisions.reason: Plenty of regions but only three colors.
decisions.suggestion: Add large multicolored wrapping motifs and contrasting broad ribbon sections.

decisions.subject: Crayons
observations: Red, yellow, green, orange, purple and turquoise occupy substantial tip, body or holder areas, providing six clear color families.
Separate crayon tips and bodies repeat several colors across large accessible shapes; the holder provides additional broad enclosed regions.
The red tip is substantial enough to paint meaningfully despite its orange wrapper; facial ink and background are excluded from palette assessment.

decisions.subject: Xylophone
observations: Substantial red, yellow, green, cyan and dark-blue bars, a purple mallet head and broad wooden parts provide varied meaningful paintable areas.
Yellow repeats on a bar and mallet head; wooden supports and two mallet shafts repeat across distinct components.
Large bars and round mallet heads preserve recognizable musical-toy appeal; white fasteners and neighboring wood shades are not needed to justify palette variety.
